title: Eight Is Great
lede: A bank set a target of eight products per household. The metric counted every account its staff opened, including the ones customers never asked for. When a measure becomes a target, it stops measuring.

commit.title: YOUR GUESS
commit.prompt: Of every 1,000 accounts opened, how many did customers never authorise?

chapters.eyebrow: THE COUNT · ONE MARK PER ACCOUNT
chapters.title: A thousand accounts

captions: Target: 8 products per customer. Your team is hitting it.
One bank ran on that exact target. Your guess first.
Of 1,000 accounts opened, how many were never authorised?
Feb 2015: 6.13 on average. One household in four had 8+.
2016: 2.1 M accounts flagged. 5,300 fired. $185 M fines.
2017: the full review says 3.5 M. 2020: $3 B to settle.
165 M accounts opened, 2009 to 2016. Here are 1,000.
The metric counted every one as a product sold.
The review flagged 21. The metric still counted them.
Your guess, outlined. The review found 21.
21 is the floor. Unused products sold were counted too.
Monday: what could move this number with nothing behind it?
Limits: 3.5 M is an estimate. One bank, one metric.

brand.takeaway: When a measure becomes a target, it stops measuring.

sources: Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, Consent Order, In the Matter of Wells Fargo Bank, N.A., File No. 2016-CFPB-0015, 8 September 2016, and press release of the same day ($100 M penalty; OCC $35 M; Los Angeles $50 M).
Independent Directors of the Board of Wells Fargo & Company, Sales Practices Investigation Report, 10 April 2017 (Shearman & Sterling LLP).
Wells Fargo & Company, "Wells Fargo Reports Completion of Expanded Third-Party Review of Retail Banking Accounts", press release, 31 August 2017 (Form 8-K, Exhibit 99.1).

U.S. Department of Justice, "Wells Fargo Agrees to Pay $3 Billion to Resolve Criminal and Civil Investigations into Sales Practices Involving the Opening of Millions of Accounts without Customer Authorization", 21 February 2020, with the Deferred Prosecution Agreement, Exhibit A, Statement of Facts.
Wells Fargo & Company, Form 10-Q for the quarter ended 31 March 2015 (retail banking household cross-sell 6.13 in February 2015; goal of eight; one in four households with eight or more).

M. Strathern, "'Improving ratings': audit in the British University system", European Review 5(3), 1997, 305-321; after C. A. E. Goodhart, "Problems of Monetary Management: The U.K. Experience", Reserve Bank of Australia, 1975.
honest: 3.5 M is the bank's review estimate (it may include some authorised accounts and misses unwanted products sold with consent); one bank and one metric, not proof that every target goes bad.

knobs_doc.name: hookT0
knobs_doc.what: s: second the first of the 8 slots starts to fill in HOOK (later = slower open)

knobs_doc.name: hookStep
knobs_doc.what: s: gap between one slot starting to fill and the next in HOOK (bigger = slower count to eight)

knobs_doc.name: slotSize
knobs_doc.what: px: edge of one household slot (bigger = heavier row; keep below slotPitch)

knobs_doc.name: slotPitch
knobs_doc.what: px: slot-to-slot distance in the household row (bigger = wider row, wider ruler)

knobs_doc.name: rowX
knobs_doc.what: px: left edge of the household row and its ruler on the film sheet (bigger = further right)

knobs_doc.name: rulerTick
knobs_doc.what: px: distance between fine ticks on the travelling ruler (bigger = fewer, calmer ticks)

knobs_doc.name: rulerOp
knobs_doc.what: opacity of the ruler's edge and ticks (lower = fainter ruler)

knobs_doc.name: rulerW
knobs_doc.what: px: stroke width of the ruler's top edge (bigger = bolder straightedge)

knobs_doc.name: gridPitch
knobs_doc.what: px: centre-to-centre distance of the 1,000 marks (bigger = larger grid; keep gridSize below it)

knobs_doc.name: gridSize
knobs_doc.what: px: edge of one mark in the 1,000 grid (bigger = denser grid, smaller gap)

knobs_doc.name: scanT0
knobs_doc.what: s: second the ruler starts its scan down the grid (the metric counting)

knobs_doc.name: scanDur
knobs_doc.what: s: length of the ruler's scan down the grid (bigger = slower sweep)

knobs_doc.name: flagT0
knobs_doc.what: s: second the first flagged mark turns red (later = review lands later)

knobs_doc.name: flagStep
knobs_doc.what: s: gap between one flagged mark turning red and the next (bigger = slower review)

knobs_doc.name: gatherT0
knobs_doc.what: s: second the red marks start to gather into the first slots

knobs_doc.name: gatherDur
knobs_doc.what: s: travel time of one mark during the gather (bigger = slower, calmer)

knobs_doc.name: guessT0
knobs_doc.what: s: second the graphite outline of the viewer's guess starts to draw

knobs_doc.name: guessDur
knobs_doc.what: s: time the guess outline takes to draw round its perimeter (bigger = slower)

knobs_doc.name: ratioT0
knobs_doc.what: s: second the ratio line appears, after the count and the guess

knobs_doc.name: floorT0
knobs_doc.what: s: second the 979 ink marks begin to ease back, leaving the floor of red

knobs_doc.name: floorOp
knobs_doc.what: opacity the ink marks settle to in the floor phase (lower = red stands out more)

knobs_doc.name: monGrid
knobs_doc.what: opacity the grid fades to under the Monday question (lower = cleaner card)

knobs_doc.name: typeCps
knobs_doc.what: characters per second the ledger lines type on in CASE (bigger = faster)
